editorial_note: Ten hours since the morning edition, a quiet Saturday, and ==no new frontier model==. The window was widened back to 21:00 on Friday to pick up two stories the morning edition missed: Thinking Machines' laptop-sized open model ==Inkling 2 Mini==, and Etsy's promise to revise its AI-training terms after sellers closed their shops. Overnight in Geneva, UN weapons talks ended with a ==two-year mandate== to draft rules on autonomous weapons, without agreeing that those rules will be binding.

stories.headline: Thinking Machines releases Inkling 2 Mini, a 26-billion-parameter open-weights model small enough to run on a 32GB Mac
paragraphs: Thinking Machines Lab released ==Inkling 2 Mini== on Friday, an open-weights model under the ==Apache 2.0 licence== that it says is small enough to run on a laptop. The weights are on Hugging Face, the model is on the company's Tinker platform, and Ollama lists it for Macs with ==32GB or more of memory==. It was first posted to Hacker News at 21:12 Paris time on Friday, after the previous afternoon edition had closed, and the morning edition did not carry it.

Inkling 2 Mini is a mixture-of-experts model with ==26.4 billion total parameters== and 3.4 billion active per token. It is a looped transformer: the middle 12 of its 24 layers run three times for every token, which the company says lets it reason more without writing more tokens. Most of its weights were trained and ship in 4-bit NVFP4, for a memory footprint of about 20GB.

Thinking Machines says the model leads every open-weights model under 100 billion parameters on DeepSWE v1.1 (48.2%) and Vals Index v2.2 (46.5%). It also says the model is weaker on multi-turn chat and on instructions with many constraints, where it trails Qwen3.8-27B. Artificial Analysis, which tests models independently, placed it at ==20 on its Intelligence Index==, level with Qwen3.8 27B, at $0.59 per task against $3.53.

The lab also released a research variant with a variable number of loops, used to test whether looping hides reasoning from people reading a model's chain of thought. It reports that the chain of thought got shorter with more loops but stayed legible, and that the model did not score higher on tests of agentic sabotage as loops were added.
stories.why_it_matters: Editorial analysis: a ==looped transformer good enough for agentic coding== at laptop size is a new design point for open weights; tests beyond one index will show whether the benchmark lead holds.
stories.caveat: The benchmark results are Thinking Machines' own, except the Artificial Analysis index. The release page gives only the date; the time comes from the first Hacker News post.

stories.headline: UN weapons talks end with a two-year mandate to draft rules on autonomous weapons, but no commitment that they will be binding
paragraphs: The 128 states party to the UN ==Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons== agreed in Geneva at about 04:45 Paris time on Saturday to 'elaborate' an international instrument on lethal autonomous weapons systems ==over the next two years==. The review conference had met since Monday; talks on the final wording ran through the night after Russian objections over procedure led to some formal sessions being called off, diplomats told Al Jazeera.

Close to 100 states had backed legally binding rules on weapons that can kill without a human making the final decision. A group of seven, Austria, Belgium, Brazil, Ireland, Mexico, New Zealand and Panama, wanted a treaty negotiated within a year. Decisions require consensus, and the United States, Russia and Israel opposed binding rules, Al Jazeera and CNA reported. Some states rejected the word 'negotiate', so the text says 'elaborate', and ==whether the result will bind anyone is left open==.

UN disarmament chief Izumi Nakamitsu called the outcome a 'significant achievement' and said 'the path to or possibility to have a legally binding instrument is still open'. A group of governmental experts will recommend the instrument's legal form, including whether it should be a binding protocol. The International Committee of the Red Cross said it regretted the lack of a clear negotiating mandate, and the Stop Killer Robots coalition called the mandate 'watered down'.

Separately, US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent told CNBC on Friday that Presidents Trump and Xi had agreed at their Shenzhen meeting that humans should always be involved in military decisions made with AI, Reuters reported. No written text of that agreement was found.
stories.why_it_matters: Editorial analysis: the forum that has discussed autonomous weapons for more than a decade now has a ==2028 horizon but no guarantee of binding rules==, while campaigners say such weapons are already in use.
stories.caveat: The agreed mandate text was not found online; its terms here come from the conference chair and UN officials as reported by news agencies. Reports put the close between 04:30 and 05:00 Geneva time.

stories.headline: Etsy says it will revise new terms that let it and its partners train AI on sellers' work, after shops close in protest
paragraphs: Etsy told The New York Times on Friday that it would revise its new Terms of Use, which take effect on ==16 December== and add a right for Etsy and its 'third party partners and vendors' to use sellers' content to 'develop, train, test and improve artificial intelligence and machine learning technologies'. The Verge reported the planned revision at 23:50 Paris time on Friday, after the previous afternoon edition had closed.

Several long-time sellers had closed their shops over the clause, the Times reported, among them an illustrator who had sold on the site for nearly a decade and a home goods and stationery brand with 13 years there. Etsy's vice-president for customer operations, James Ossman, said the company would ==share the revised terms directly with sellers soon== and that their creative work belongs to them.

Earlier in the week, in a post on Etsy's community site, Ossman wrote that Etsy does not use seller content 'to train AI models designed to copy your original work or replace your creativity'. He listed its current uses as fraud detection, search and recommendations, and seller tools, and said vendors with access include fraud-detection services and advertising partners. The revised wording has ==not yet been published==.
stories.why_it_matters: Editorial analysis: Etsy is the latest platform to find that ==broad AI-training clauses can cost it the creators== whose work it sells.
stories.caveat: Etsy's promise to revise the terms was made in a statement emailed to The New York Times, read here in the Philadelphia Inquirer's syndicated copy because the Times site is paywalled. Etsy's Terms of Use page answered HTTP 403 and was not read; the clause wording comes from the Times report.
